title: FBISE Annual Exam Simulator 07 (Board Paper Standard II (Prose & Syntax))
subject: english-12

questions.question: Why does life appear so rare and precious in Jeans' cosmic analysis in 'The Dying Sun'?

options.A: Because almost all of space is either intensely hot inside stars or freezing cold in the cosmic vacuum.
options.B: Because radiation from black holes destroys all biological matter.
options.C: Because only Earth possesses gravity in the Milky Way.
options.D: Because oxygen exists only on our moon.

questions.explanation: Stars are gigantic incandescent furnaces where life would burn, and open space is near absolute zero, making hospitable temperature zones extraordinary anomalies.

questions.question: In 'The Dying Sun', what was the initial state of the planetary bodies after breaking off from the sun?

options.A: Frozen blocks of extraterrestrial ice
options.B: Glowing balls of raging gas that gradually cooled down over aeons
options.C: Solid granite continents covered in rainforests
options.D: Hollow crystalline spheres orbiting the Milky Way

questions.explanation: The planets were originally hot gases that condensed, cooled, and developed crusts over millions of years.

questions.question: In 'On Destroying Books', Squire observes that throwing books away makes people feel like they are committing:

options.A: Sacrilege or murder
options.B: High treason against the Crown
options.C: A minor civil infraction
options.D: An environmental felony

questions.explanation: People treat books as living spiritual entities, making discarding them feel akin to murder or sacrilege.

questions.question: What is the antonym of 'malady' as used in Jerome's essay?

options.A: Sickness
options.B: Affliction
options.C: Wellness / Robust health
options.D: Disorder

questions.explanation: 'Malady' means a disease or ailment; its opposite is wellness, health, or robustness.

questions.question: What is the tone of Stephen Leacock's 'My Financial Career'?

options.A: Tragic and remorseful
options.B: Farce, burlesque, and high comedy
options.C: Scholarly economics critique
options.D: Philosophical meditation

questions.explanation: Leacock is Canada's celebrated humorist, using farce and self-mockery to expose ordinary human nervousness.

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect speech: He said, 'I opened an account here yesterday.'

options.A: He said that he opened an account here yesterday.
options.B: He said that he had opened an account there the day before.
options.C: He said he has opened an account there yesterday.
options.D: He said that he opens an account there tomorrow.

questions.explanation: Past simple shifts to past perfect ('had opened'), 'here' shifts to 'there', and 'yesterday' shifts to 'the day before'.

questions.question: In 'First Year at Harrow', Mr. Somervell taught English analysis using what innovative method?

options.A: He made boys write Shakespeare plays from memory.
options.B: He divided long sentences into subject, verb, and object using different colored inks (black, red, blue, green).
options.C: He played phonograph recordings in class.
options.D: He gave tests exclusively in Latin.

questions.explanation: Mr. Somervell used a visual structural system with colored inks and brackets, making sentence syntax intuitively understandable.

questions.question: Identify the voice of the sentence: 'A heavy load of books was carried across the river by Squire.'

options.A: Active Voice
options.B: Passive Voice
options.C: Middle Voice
options.D: Imperative Mood

questions.explanation: The subject ('load') receives the action ('was carried') from the agent introduced by 'by', defining passive voice.

questions.question: What was the initial medical response when Fleming published his 1929 paper on Penicillin?

options.A: Massive global excitement and immediate commercial manufacture
options.B: Virtually complete indifference and silence, as few grasped its revolutionary therapeutic significance
options.C: He was knighted by the King the following morning
options.D: The paper was burned by medical journals

questions.explanation: The British Journal of Experimental Pathology paper attracted almost zero public interest until Florey and Chain revived it in 1939.

questions.question: How did Joseph Meister express his lifelong gratitude to Louis Pasteur?

options.A: He became the gatekeeper and caretaker of the Pasteur Institute until his death
options.B: He paid Pasteur a monthly pension
options.C: He wrote a best-selling novel about him
options.D: He named his village after Pasteur

questions.explanation: Joseph Meister served loyally as the gatekeeper of the Pasteur Institute in Paris for the rest of his life.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence featuring proper use of the idiom 'to turn a blind eye':

options.A: The Sultan turned a blind eye to Allied occupying troops taking over government ministries.
options.B: The doctor turned a blind eye with an ophthalmoscope.
options.C: The blind eye turned the wheel of the carriage.
options.D: He turned a blind eye to see the stars.

questions.explanation: 'To turn a blind eye' means deliberately ignoring something undesirable or unlawful.

questions.question: What did Kemal reply when asked why he replaced the fez with the hat?

options.A: 'A civilized, international dress is worthy and appropriate for our civilized and international nation.'
options.B: 'Because hats protect against rain better.'
options.C: 'To increase textile factory profits.'
options.D: 'Because the fez was too heavy.'

questions.explanation: Kemal stated that a civilized nation must reflect its progressive mindset in its outward attire, discarding symbols of medieval decadence.

questions.question: What kind of novel is James Hilton's 'Good-bye, Mr. Chips' classified as?

options.A: A dystopian science-fiction epic
options.B: A poignant, sentimental novella portraying Victorian and Edwardian school life, nostalgia, and personal loyalty
options.C: A gothic murder mystery
options.D: A political thriller set in Berlin

questions.explanation: The novella is a celebrated masterpiece of English school fiction, brimming with warm sentiment, gentle wit, and historical poignancy.

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect speech: Chips said, 'Colley, write a hundred lines.'

options.A: Chips ordered Colley to write a hundred lines.
options.B: Chips said that Colley should wrote a hundred lines.
options.C: Chips asked Colley if he writes a hundred lines.
options.D: Chips told to Colley to write lines.

questions.explanation: Imperative commands shift into reporting verb 'ordered/commanded' followed by infinitive 'to write'.

questions.question: How did the alumni (Old Boys) react when they heard rumors that Ralston was trying to force Chips out?

options.A: They sent letters and visited the governors, pledging total solidarity with Chips and threatening to withhold donations.
options.B: They supported Ralston unanimously.
options.C: They demanded that the school be closed.
options.D: They ignored the controversy.

questions.explanation: The Old Boys rallied fiercely behind Chips, proving that personal affection outweighed technocratic efficiency.

questions.question: Which word best describes Chips' humor in his senior years?

options.A: Sarcastic and biting
options.B: Dry, mellow, self-deprecating, and kindly
options.C: Cruel and mocking
options.D: Noisy and slapstick

questions.explanation: Chips' wit was gentle, ripe, and warm, bringing chuckles rather than stinging offense.

questions.question: What did the author James Hilton base the character of Mr. Chips upon in real life?

options.A: His own father, John Hilton (a dedicated schoolmaster), and his former Latin master, W.H. Balgarnie of The Leys School, Cambridge
options.B: Winston Churchill
options.C: Alexander Fleming
options.D: Charles Dickens

questions.explanation: Hilton drew inspiration from his schoolmaster father and his beloved Latin teacher W.H. Balgarnie, who taught at The Leys for over fifty years.

questions.question: What was the final sound that echoed across the quiet evening as Chips closed his eyes?

options.A: The chimes of the Brookfield chapel bell ringing for lights-out
options.B: The whistle of a steam train
options.C: A gunshot
options.D: Loud rock music

questions.explanation: The distant, comforting tones of the Brookfield bell tolled across the autumn air, marking the gentle close of a noble life.

questions.question: What does the idiom 'to hit below the belt' mean?

options.A: To act in an unfair, treacherous, or cowardly manner
options.B: To score a goal in football
options.C: To fasten a leather belt tightly
options.D: To wear sports padding

questions.explanation: Derived from boxing rules, hitting below the belt means striking an opponent unfairly or dishonorably.

questions.question: What is the primary SLO requirement for the FBISE Section A English paper?

options.A: Rote memorization of textbook exercise questions without context
options.B: Demonstrating conceptual comprehension of prescribed texts and applying rigorous rules of functional grammar, syntax, and rhetoric
options.C: Translating whole pages into classical Greek
options.D: Writing personal diaries during examination hours

questions.explanation: The Federal Board SLO framework evaluates analytical understanding of literary themes and practical application of standard English grammar.
